nodes.title: 提示词
widgets_values:
subject_definitions
<Subject 1> is the person in <Picture 1>. Use the image as the sole character reference, preserving the visible identity, hairstyle, clothing, and accessories without redesign.

summary
[reference generation] A ten-second, restrained period-drama scene beside a window and a warm lamp. <Subject 1> finishes reading a letter, folds it, and starts offering it to an unseen person. When she looks up, her expectation turns to hesitation. She quietly draws the letter back before anyone takes it.

retention_analysis
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved from <Picture 1> across all shots.
<Picture 1> defines the character and visible wardrobe, not a mandatory first frame, pose, background, or layout. Do not reproduce its watermark or signature.
Introduce one paper letter, one wooden table, and one shaded warm lamp as new scene props. The intended recipient stays entirely off-screen.

detailed_description
Photorealistic cinematic imagery in a quiet traditional room at dusk, with soft cool window light balanced by a steady warm lamp. Use vertical 3:4 framing, natural skin texture, clearly visible eyes, and shallow background separation; preserve the delicacy of the reference without magical effects.

[Shot 1] Begin with a seated, eye-level three-quarter medium close-up of <Subject 1> beside a wooden table. Frame her head, upper body, and hands together. The window lies to one side, while a single shaded lamp sits farther back on the table, outside her hand movements. Its warmth complements the broad window light rather than casting her face into darkness. The table is otherwise uncluttered.

During the first two seconds, she holds one small paper letter in both hands just below chest height and finishes reading its final lines. Her gaze tracks downward once, then pauses; a faint expectation softens her mouth. Keep the written side toward her so no readable text needs to appear. The letter stays below her face and does not hide her eyes or mouth.

Between two and four seconds, she folds the letter once along an existing central crease. Her left hand steadies the lower half, and her right hand closes the fold. She then holds the folded letter between her right fingers, with her left fingertips lightly supporting its lower edge, and extends it a short distance toward the unseen recipient beside the camera. Her eyes begin to lift. Keep the entire gesture gentle and purposeful, with anatomically natural hands and no extra paper or envelope.

[Shot 2] At 00:04.000, cut to a facial close-up on the same side of the eyeline. She meets the unseen person's gaze just beside the lens. For a brief moment she waits, still expecting a response. No response arrives. Her eyes search subtly, the suggestion of a smile fades, and her lips part slightly before closing again. She does not cry or suddenly look angry. Her hands remain extended below the crop, still holding the same folded letter. The camera stays nearly still, allowing the change from hope to restraint to become readable.

[Shot 3] At 00:07.000, cut back to the original medium close-up, preserving the extended letter and hand positions. She lowers her gaze first, then deliberately draws both hands back toward herself. The other person never touches the letter. She brings it to rest in her hands just above the table edge, places her left fingertips over the fold, and releases one quiet breath. End with the letter still held close and her expression composed but unresolved. Use only a minimal, slow forward camera movement over this final shot; all performance remains at normal real-time speed.

Preserve character identity, paper size, single fold, lamp position, and lighting across cuts. No dialogue, extra people or hands, handover, tearing or burning the letter, dramatic sobbing, forced smile, slow motion, freeze frame, subtitles, logos, or watermark.

overall_soundscape
Quiet room ambience, a faint breeze beyond the window, delicate paper rustling during the single fold, and one restrained exhale as she withdraws the letter. The pause after she looks up remains unanswered. No intelligible speech.

non_diegetic_music
N/A
